claims.claim: The planar dual T of G is a simple Eulerian plane triangulation with a proper vertex 3-colouring I1,I2,I3, unique up to permuting the colours.
claims.evidence: Choose the polyhedral plane embedding supplied by 3-connectivity. Its dual is simple, every dual face is triangular because G is cubic, and every dual degree is an even primal face length because G is bipartite. Colouring one facial triangle and propagating across adjacent triangles is consistent around each even-degree vertex and hence yields a proper 3-colouring. Connectedness of the facial-adjacency graph makes every subsequent colour forced, proving uniqueness up to the six initial colour permutations.

claims.claim: For each colour i, the boundaries of the primal faces corresponding to Ii are pairwise vertex-disjoint cycles covering V(G). Moreover, each colour class has total face perimeter n=|V(G)|, G has n/2+2 faces, and it has at least six quadrilateral faces.
claims.evidence: The three faces incident with any primal vertex form a facial triangle of T and therefore have all three colours. Thus exactly one face of each colour contains each vertex, proving disjointness, coverage, and perimeter n. Cubicity gives |E|=3n/2, so Euler's formula gives |F|=n/2+2. Hence sum_f(6-|f|)=6|F|-2|E|=12. Face lengths are even and at least four; quadrilaterals contribute 2 and every other face contributes at most zero, so there are at least six quadrilaterals.
claims.search_method: Exact incidence counting and Euler's formula.

claims.claim: G is Hamiltonian if and only if V(T) can be partitioned into two sets inducing forests.
claims.evidence: Let N=|V(T)|. Under a two-forest partition every triangular face has two cross edges. Counting face-edge incidences gives 2N-4 cross edges and therefore N-2 internal edges. If the induced forests have cX and cY components, their internal-edge total is N-cX-cY, forcing cX=cY=1. The primal edges dual to the cross edges form a spanning 2-factor. If it has k cycles, its complement on the sphere has k+1 regions, whereas the two internal dual trees give exactly two regions; hence k=1. Conversely, a Hamiltonian cycle partitions primal faces into its two sides. Each side's induced dual is connected, and the n/2 noncycle primal edges give N-2 internal dual edges in total, exactly the minimum for two connected graphs; both induced graphs are therefore trees.
claims.search_method: Bidirectional dual edge count and Jordan-curve region argument.

claims.claim: If any bichromatic graph H=T[Ii union Ij] has a CAI-partition, then G is Hamiltonian.
claims.evidence: Write the CAI-partition as A union J and let Ik be the omitted colour. If T[J union Ik] contained a cycle C, connectedness of A would place A wholly on one side of C. On the other side, consecutive neighbours of a boundary vertex produce a facial triangle contained in J union Ik, impossible because J and Ik are independent. Thus T[J union Ik] is a forest, while T[A] is a tree. Claim 2 then supplies a Hamiltonian cycle.
claims.search_method: Direct verification of the planar CAI-to-two-forest reduction.

claims.claim: In particular, G is Hamiltonian whenever some bichromatic graph T[Ii union Ij] is series-parallel.
claims.evidence: Each bichromatic graph is simple and 2-vertex-connected. The supplied source proves that every simple 2-vertex-connected series-parallel graph has a CAI-partition via a short nested open-ear decomposition: the independent-set choices leave each new ear attached to the existing induced tree without a cycle, while nesting and inducedness exclude unwanted adjacencies. Claim 3 then applies. All hypotheses of that theorem match H.
claims.search_method: Checked theorem statement, ear-decomposition proof, and applicability against the supplied source.

claims.claim: For distinct colours i,j, let Qij have the i-coloured faces as vertices, with one edge for every j-coloured quadrilateral joining the two i-coloured faces opposite it. Then G has a spanning 2-factor with exactly c(Qij) cycles. In particular, connected Qij certifies Hamiltonicity.
claims.evidence: Start with the facial 2-factor of colour i. At a j-coloured quadrilateral its boundary alternates between two selected and two unselected edges, and its two incident i-faces are distinct. Symmetric difference with that boundary therefore merges their two current cycles. Quadrilaterals of colour j are vertex-disjoint, so switches cannot interfere. Selecting a spanning forest of Qij ensures each switch joins two different current components. Starting with |V(Qij)| cycles and performing |V(Qij)|-c(Qij) merges leaves exactly c(Qij) cycles.
claims.search_method: Invariant proof for symmetric-difference switches along an auxiliary spanning forest.

claims.claim: Every target graph on n vertices has a spanning 2-factor with at most floor((n+4)/6)-1 cycles.
claims.evidence: Let a be the smallest face-colour-class size. Since there are n/2+2 faces, a is at most floor((n+4)/6). If a=1, that face boundary is Hamiltonian. Otherwise at least one of the other two colours contains a quadrilateral: if neither did, each would contain at most n/6 faces, and minimality would give the same bound for a, contradicting the total n/2+2. That quadrilateral gives a nonloop edge in the appropriate Qij, so Qij has at most a-1 components. Claim 5 gives the asserted 2-factor bound.
claims.search_method: Integer face-count bound followed by the auxiliary-component construction.

claims.claim: Let H be 2-vertex-connected. Suppress its maximal degree-2 paths to a multigraph K, let B be the vertices of degree at least three, and let U=H[B], the unsubdivided skeleton edges. If U is a forest, or U-v is a forest for some v in B, then H has a CAI-partition.
claims.evidence: If H is a cycle, one removed vertex is the independent set and the complement is a path. Otherwise, when U is a forest, extend it to a spanning tree R of K. Every non-R skeleton edge is subdivided, so choose one internal vertex from each corresponding path. These choices are independent, and their deletion leaves the subdivided R plus pendant path fragments, hence an induced tree. If U-v is a forest, 2-connectivity makes K-v connected; extend U-v to a spanning tree there, include v in the independent set, and choose internal vertices only from non-tree paths not incident with v. Paths incident with v become pendant after deleting v. The same independence and induced-tree conclusions follow.
claims.search_method: Constructive proof on the suppressed skeleton, including the cycle and special-vertex cases.

claims.claim: In any counterexample, every face-colour class contains at least three nonquadrilateral faces; for every colour pair, their nonquadrilateral-face adjacency graph has feedback-vertex number at least two. Moreover, every Qij is disconnected and every bichromatic graph is non-series-parallel.
claims.evidence: In a bichromatic graph, a face of length 2d has degree d, so its degree-at-least-three vertices are exactly the nonquadrilateral faces and their induced graph is U from claim 7. Feedback-vertex number at most one would make U or U-v a forest, yielding a CAI-partition and then Hamiltonicity. If one bipartition class of U had at most one vertex it would be acyclic; if it had exactly two, deleting either vertex would destroy every simple bipartite cycle. Thus every face-colour class has at least three such faces. Claims 5 and 4 respectively force every Qij to be disconnected and every bichromatic graph to be non-series-parallel in a counterexample.
claims.search_method: Contrapositive application of the verified sufficient conditions and bipartite cycle analysis.

claims.claim: If two face-colour classes each consist of exactly three hexagons together with any number of quadrilaterals, then G is Hamiltonian.
claims.evidence: For their bichromatic graph H, the six branch vertices are the hexagons and form a 3-by-3 bipartite graph U. If H lacked a CAI-partition, claim 7 would force U-v to contain a cycle for every vertex v. The exact checker examined all 512 Boolean adjacency matrices and found precisely K3,3 and its nine one-edge deletions. K3,3 is nonplanar. In K3,3 minus one edge, four branch vertices are already saturated at degree three; the two missing-edge endpoints have one remaining incidence each, so every degree-2 vertex lies on a path joining them. Thus H is a subdivision of K3,3, again contradicting planarity. Hence H has a CAI-partition and claim 3 proves Hamiltonicity. The checker exited successfully with qualifying edge counts 8:9 and 9:1.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive exact Boolean enumeration of all 512 matrices, followed by degree-saturation and planarity arguments.

claims.claim: Every graph satisfying the target assumptions with at most 30 vertices is Hamiltonian; consequently these arguments force every counterexample to have at least 32 vertices.
claims.evidence: Put n=2m and define qi, ri, si as in the draft. Exact perimeter and face counts give 2qi+3ri+si=m and r+s=m-4. Claim 8 gives ri at least 3 in a counterexample. The integer checker exhaustively enumerated every resulting profile for m=2 through 15: there are no candidates through m=12, one at m=13, none at m=14, and nine at m=15. Every m=13 or m=15 candidate has at least two classes with (ri,si)=(3,0), meaning exactly three hexagons and otherwise quadrilaterals. Claim 9 then proves Hamiltonicity. Since cubic graphs have even order, any counterexample surviving these arguments has at least 32 vertices.
claims.search_method: Exact integer enumeration of all necessary face profiles through half-order 15, combined with claims 8 and 9.

target_evidence: The exact target demands either a proof that every graph satisfying (i)-(iv) is Hamiltonian or one explicit qualifying non-Hamiltonian graph with proof. The draft supplies neither and explicitly says that no full resolution or counterexample is claimed. Its verified dual criteria, universal 2-factor bound, structural obstructions, and proof of Hamiltonicity through 30 vertices are material but incomplete progress. The headline claimed_resolution of PARTIAL therefore matches the independently established coverage and is neither overstated nor understated.
